content: What is a keyboard if not the original brain-computer interface? You can tap on a touchscreen or talk to the computer, but if your work involves getting information out of your head and into the computer, you’re probably spending a lot of time using a keyboard. We’ve written about many keyboards over the years, from the legendary Optimus Maximus to the ultra-luxe Seneca to even stranger fare. But I wanted to know what my coworkers actually use. As I’d hoped, there’s a wide range. Some of us are strictly utilitarian, optimizing for ergonomics or functionality. Others obsess over every detail of feel, sound, layout, and looks. Still others — maybe the most enlightened — just use whatever’s in front of them. NuPhy came up a lot. So did Keychron. The Apple Magic Keyboard has its stalwarts. The Kinesis Freestyle split is surprisingly well represented. And there are other, odder entries. These are the keyboards of The Verge. In this article Jay Peters, senior reporter [Image: Jay Peters’ Kinesis Freestyle Pro in a picture from 2021. Sadly, Gouda the cat passed away, but his spirit lives on through this photo. https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/chorus/uploads/chorus_asset/file/22347076/jpeters_210301_4457_0020.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] I currently use the Kinesis Freestyle Pro, and I’ve used it for so long that I’ve forgotten when I first got it. In the late 2010s, I had wrist pain that led me to try a lot of ergonomic keyboards so I could keep using computers. The Freestyle Pro — with its optional tenting add-ons that give the keyboard a significant angle and the palm rest accessories — just feels the best under my hands. If this keyboard broke, I’d buy another one the same day. Kallie Plagge, senior copy editor [Product: Logitech G713 wired mechanical keyboard and wristrest | https://www.amazon.com/Logitech-G-Wired-Gaming-Keyboard/dp/B092LK5NSN/ref=sr_1_1?tag=theverge02-20, https://logitech.cfzu.net/c/482924/499820/8585?u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.logitechg.com%2Fen-us%2Fproducts%2Fgaming-keyboards%2Fg713-tkl-mechanical-gaming-keyboard.html] For work, I use a simple Keychron K2. But for my gaming PC, I use the Logitech G713 wired mechanical keyboard — the one that comes with the cloud wrist rest. Did I mostly buy it for the wrist rest? Perhaps. But I do love the tenkeyless layout. My previous gaming keyboard had a number pad and two rows of programmable keys, which was cool, but I mostly used the number pad to type the alt code for em dashes. The G713, on the other hand, meets my gaming requirements without taking up half my desk. I’m not playing anything competitive on my PC that requires adjustable actuation points, so the GX red linear switches do the trick. (And they’re the right amount of clicky, unlike the overly loud ones on my K2.) So yeah, maybe I bought it for the sleek all-white look and the cute wrist rest, but it’s also a great keyboard, too. Danielle Steussy, product manager [Product: Apple Magic Keyboard with Touch ID and Numeric Keypad | https://www.amazon.com/Keyboard-Numeric-Keypad-Apple-Silicon/dp/B0DL6L189W?tag=theverge02-20, https://bestbuy.7tiv.net/c/482924/614286/10014?u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.bestbuy.com%2Fproduct%2Fmagic-keyboard-with-touch-id-and-numeric-keypad-for-mac-models-with-apple-silicon-usb-c-black-keys%2FJJGCQ8CV73] I’m using Apple’s Magic Keyboard with the numeric keypad. Some version of Apple’s keyboard has been on my desk for over 20 years, starting with the Apple A1048 that came with my first Mac in college. I loved that keyboard (the sound of my fingertips hitting the keys — swoon!) and I wore it down to the point of keys falling off. Since then, I’ve stuck with Apple’s wireless keyboards. Honestly, it’s a pretty keyboard, but otherwise unremarkable, and blends in with my desk setup (which also is kind of the point, right?). My biggest complaints are that the key legends wear off faster than I’d like and the Bluetooth connection isn’t totally reliable. It’s not my favorite Apple product (by far), but after two decades of muscle memory, I’m not switching anytime soon. David Pierce, editor at large I really want to be a mechanical keyboard guy. I love typing on mechanical keyboards! I love the clackiness, the way they look on my desk, the huge personality upgrade that comes with them. But then I start typing notes during a call, and someone goes, “Sorry, what’s that noise in the background?” and I bail on my mechanical keyboard. I used Logitech’s MX Keys S for the last few years, and love that keyboard, but recently replaced it with an Apple Magic Keyboard (black keys, number pad) because I got tired of typing my 1Password password all the time. I bought a $200 keyboard for the Touch ID button. Ugh. Jacob Kastrenakes, executive editor [Image: Come on, you know where the letters are. https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/Boopdots.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] My keyboard is probably the single dumbest thing I have ever spent money on, but it brings me joy every time I look at it. The setup matches a Boop Redux case with the GMK Dots keycaps and Silent Bluish White (V2) switches. I didn’t so much want to get deep into the mechanical keyboard hobby as I wanted to have this exact keyboard after I saw images of the Dots keycaps on the (original) Boop case floating around in around 2022. It looks cool, right? (Right?) From a practical standpoint, this is fully a downgrade from the Apple Magic Keyboard I was using before: It’s bigger and louder, with fewer keys, and I probably type a bit slower on it, too, owing to the longer key strokes. It’s also a few hundred dollars more expensive. But you know what? I think it looks really cool. Antonio G. Di Benedetto, laptop reviewer [Image: I’ve changed the keycaps and switches on this TM680 so many times. https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/IMG_7469.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] Since I review laptops and occasionally mechanical keyboards, I’m constantly changing

chineseContent: 如果键盘不是原始的脑机接口，那它是什么？您可以点击触摸屏或与计算机交谈，但如果您的工作涉及将信息从大脑中提取到计算机中，那么您可能会花费大量时间使用键盘。多年来，我们写过许多键盘，从传奇的 Optimus Maximus 到超豪华的 Seneca，再到更奇怪的键盘。但我想知道我的同事实际使用什么。正如我所希望的，范围很广。我们中的一些人是严格功利主义者，针对人体工程学或功能进行优化。其他人则着迷于感觉、声音、布局和外观的每一个细节。还有一些人——也许是最开明的——只是使用他们面前的任何东西。 NuPhy 出现了很多。 Keychron 也是如此。苹果妙控键盘有它的坚定支持者。 Kinesis Freestyle 的表现出人意料地出色。还有其他更奇怪的条目。这些是 The Verge 的键盘。在这篇文章中，资深记者 Jay Peters [图片：Jay Peters 的 Kinesis Freestyle Pro 在 2021 年的一张照片中。遗憾的是，Gouda 猫去世了，但他的精神通过这张照片永存。 https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/chorus/uploads/chorus_asset/file/22347076/jpeters_210301_4457_0020.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] 我目前使用 Kinesis Freestyle Pro，并且已经使用了很长时间，以至于我已经忘记了第一次拿到它的时间。在 2010 年代末，我的手腕疼痛让我尝试了很多符合人体工程学的键盘，这样我就可以继续使用电脑。 Freestyle Pro 配有可选的帐篷附加组件，可为键盘提供显着的角度，还有掌托配件，在我的手下感觉最好。如果这个键盘坏了，我会在同一天再买一个。 Kallie Plagge，高级文案编辑【产品：罗技 G713 有线机械键盘】
